hwe_bench.problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's backend floating-point fused multiply-add (FMA) path, an instruction can use the wrong rounding mode (`rm`) after its multiply stage completes. If the external `rm` input changes before the add stage consumes the intermediate result, the FMA may be rounded using the newer mode instead of the mode that was present when the instruction was issued, so the final value can be wrong. Expected behavior: an FMA must keep its original `rm` for the entire operation. When an instruction is issued under one rounding mode and the `rm` input changes before the add stage, the completed result must still match the rounding mode captured at issue time. Affected function: the backend FPU FMA unit, specifically the handoff from the multiply stage to the add stage. Trigger condition: a multi-stage FMA is in flight and the `rm` input changes between the mul and add stages, especially on operands where different rounding modes produce different final results.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Capture rm_i at issue_i and report that captured mode when complete_i finishes the same in-flight operation.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A multi-stage FMA could use a newer live rounding mode in its add stage instead of the mode present when the instruction issued.
